name: Coreference Chain Resolution
description: Analyzes the length and complexity of entity tracking chains (how often pronouns successfully refer back to a distant proper noun) to detect shallow cognitive modeling.
algorithm: Neural Coreference Tracking & Entity Chain Scoring
mechanism: Human writers maintain complex, long-term mental models of the subjects they write about. We confidently introduce an entity (e.g., 'Alexander the Great') in paragraph one, and comfortably refer back to him as 'he', 'the conqueror', or 'his' several paragraphs later, creating a deep 'coreference chain'. Autoregressive AI models, bound by context windows and lacking an actual 'memory' of the narrative structure, struggle with this. To avoid ambiguous pronoun resolution, a well-aligned AI will conservatively 'reset' the chain by continually re-stating the proper noun (e.g., mentioning 'Alexander the Great' again in paragraph three instead of 'he'). This method deploys a neural coreference resolver to map every entity mention and its corresponding pronouns across the text. An AI-generated document typically exhibits pathologically short, fractured coreference chains, indicating a surface-level, stateless generation process that lacks deep object permanence.
useCase: Exposing synthetic origins in long-form essays, short stories, and historical analyses where the AI awkwardly over-repeats character or abstract entity names instead of trusting the reader to follow complex pronoun chains.
strengths:
• Captures deep, discourse-level coherence failures that are invisible to superficial syntactic or lexical checkers.
• Highly effective against advanced models that have mastered local sentence grammar but still fail at document-level structural memory.
• Immune to basic spelling or synonym-spinning evasion strategies.
limitations:
• Exceedingly expensive to compute, requiring a dedicated neural network just to map the entity chains before analysis can even begin.
• Short texts (under 200 words) yield too few chains to form a statistically significant profile.
• Can produce false positives on highly technical or legal documents where human authors are legally required to avoid pronouns and repeat proper nouns to prevent ambiguity.
parameters:
Analysis: Neural Coreference Mapping
Metric: Chain Density, Average Referential Distance, and Branching Factor
Output: 0-100 Shallow Referential Tracking Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-85%. Exhibits lethal precision on long-form narrative texts and essays mapping complex noun interactions.

references.title: Dugan, L. et al. (2024). RAID: A Shared Benchmark for Robust Evaluation of Machine-Generated Text Detectors. ACL.
Clark, K. & Manning, C. D. (2016). Deep Reinforcement Learning for Mention-Ranking Coreference Models. EMNLP.
